newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW-Small deals due, Q4 pricing seen sober.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-Small deals due, Q4 pricing seen sober.

text.p: A buyer's market for initial public offerings (IPOs) is forecast for the rest of the year, allowing small investors to buy into newly public companies at sober prices.

About 10 small-sized firms plan market debuts this week and only two went public last week. Large underwriters are sticking to the sidelines, preparing to unleash a torrent of deals in late September and October.

"There's not many deals this week, and they're small-cap deals by small underwriters. The major players just aren't in there yet," said John Fitzgibbon, of the IPO Aftermarket. Analysts called the upcoming weekly snooze was typical for the IPO market after the Labor Day holiday.

"Things should start to take off in mid to late September. Lots of deals taken off the summer calendar during the market slowdown are coming, and lots of companies are out on the road now," said Dara Podber, at Unterberg Harris syndicate.
Firms often travel around before offerings, hosting "road shows" in major cities to woo potential investors.
Over 300 companies have registered to raise money on Wall Street in upcoming public offerings, according to David Menlow of the IPO Financial Network, based in Springfield, N.J.
"I'm not sure the marketplace will allow for the completion of many of these, but where there's a will there's often a way," said Robert Natale of Standard & Poor's.

"I don't think you'll see aggressive pricing. It's a neutral environment for new issues. Interest rate concerns will be in place for some time and I don't see economic growth tailing off significantly over the next 6 months. That's going to keep a lid on stock prices," Natale said.
"There is still money flowing in, albeit at a slower rate, so many deals should get done. But I don't see a return to the euphoric days of the past spring," Natale said.

Menlow agreed: "For the balance of the year, we will be in a very advantageous posture for investors. Premiums will be there to point a direction to where the big money is going, but they won't be out of control."

"So a small investor, although they may not be able to get in on the IPO, will have a good chance to buy in the aftermarket," he said. "It's now more important to get the deals done and show a better balance between value for the issuer and value for the investors."

Coffee shop chain Diedrich Coffee is due to make its market debut as well as American Craft Brewing International Ltd, which operates an American style microbrewery in Hong Kong called the South China Brewery.

Cable-Sat Systems, which allows users to send color faxes from computers equipped with Cable-Sat software, is planning to raise about $6 million in a public offering underwritten by Barron Chase. Also coming to market are St. Joseph Capital Corp, Thermo Fibergen Inc, and Ensec International Inc.

Natale also said retail and energy IPOs could get a boost because their market sectors are currently in favor with Wall Street. Houston Exploration and retailer Abercrombie & Fitch both plan September offerings.
